subject: POC prompt set & eval plan - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@acmecorp.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC prompt set & eval plan - next steps

Thanks again for the call today - great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned before the POC kickoff:

Summary / success criteria (as discussed)
- Accuracy: our model should match AcmeCorp's expected answer for >= 85% of production-like prompts across primary intents.
- Safety & data handling: no leakage of PII; processing must comply with your policies.
- Latency: sub-500ms 95th percentile for interactive Q&A workload (we'll measure during dedicated runs).
- Business metric: reduce average handle time for support triage by 25% in the POC scope (validated via sampled logs).

What we need from you to run the evaluation
1) Prompt set / logs: a representative sample (preferred: CSV or JSONL). Columns we typically use: prompt_id, prompt_text, context, expected_response (if available), confidence, source_log_id. Approximately 200-500 prompts across top intents + ~50 negative/error cases. If you have raw logs, we can take them and help label a subset.
2) Expected outputs / oracle labels: for a seed of ~30-50 examples please include the 'expected_response' if you have it - this helps calibrate automatic matching rules.
3) PII guidance: please sanitize or replace PII with placeholders (e.g., [EMAIL], [SSN]) but keep enough context so intents remain valid.
4) Delivery mechanism: Drive link, S3 presigned URL, or secure SFTP - whichever is easiest.

Timeline
- Please share the prompt/log sample by EOD Thu Mar 5 (so our SE team can prepare the eval harness).
- POC kickoff: week of Mar 8.
- Eval run & initial report: within 3 business days after we receive the dataset.

Ownership
- Acme contacts: Sam (technical lead) and Priya (product owner).
- Redwood: me (POC lead) and Aditya (SE / evaluation lead).

I've attached a short eval plan (acme_poc_eval_plan_v1.pdf) that outlines the metrics and the two model configurations we'll test (baseline vs optimized). Please confirm owners and let me know if there are any constraints (PII, redaction, export controls) we should be aware of before you share data.

Thanks - looking forward to getting the dataset and kicking this off.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. We're aligned on the success criteria. I've attached a small sample CSV (acmecorp_prompt_samples.csv) that follows the columns you suggested. A few notes:

- The current sample contains ~140 prompts drawn from our support logs and product FAQs; we can expand to 300+ by EOD Thu.
- Expected_response is present for ~40 examples. For the remainder we can provide a short label or leave blank and mark for human review.
- Some log rows contain PII (customer emails and account ids). We will sanitize before delivery, replacing values with placeholders. Our security team prefers SFTP or an enterprise Drive folder over public presigned URLs.

Question: what format do you need for context when a prompt references a prior message thread? Do you prefer a single concatenated context field or multiple context_* columns?

I'll coordinate with Priya and try to get the larger dataset to you by Thu. If we can send via SFTP, please share connection details or a secure upload location.

Thanks,
Sam Turner

Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC prompt set & eval plan - next steps

Thanks Sam - that works. Quick answers: we prefer a single "context" field that concatenates prior turns (up to ~3 previous messages) - keeps the eval harness simpler. If you need to send raw message arrays, JSONL is fine too; we'll accept either CSV or JSONL.

Minimum requirements for the dataset we'll run through the automated eval:
- Fields: prompt_id, prompt_text, context (optional), expected_response (optional), source_log_id
- Volume: target 200+ production-like prompts covering top 6 intents, plus ~50 negative/failure cases (bad parses, out-of-scope, ambiguous queries)
- Label guidance: if you can provide expected_response for at least 30 examples, that speeds up metric tuning.
- PII: replace with placeholders; preserve entity markers like [PRODUCT_NAME] or [ORDER_ID].

If possible, include notes on how your team ranks answers (e.g., helpful / partially_helpful / not_helpful) - we can map that to a pass/fail threshold.

We'll set up the eval harness as soon as we receive the files. If SFTP is preferred, Neha (cc'd) will share our secure upload details - Neha, can you confirm?

Thanks - Marissa

Hi Sam / Marissa - quick note from the SE side on how we'll operationalize the eval once we have the data:

Planned evaluation approach
- Automatic matching: we'll run string/semantic matching against expected_response where present (we use a combination of exact, token-overlap, and embedding-similarity thresholds). Primary metric: pass_rate (matches / total). Secondary: mean_similarity score.
- Human review: we'll sample ~100 responses across intents for manual labeling (helpful / not_helpful) to validate automatic thresholds.
- Configs: we'll run two configs - your baseline (current model) and optimized config (quantized + batching + KV caching).

What we need from Acme
- Oracle labels for at least 30 examples (any format) so we can tune matching rules.
- Confirmation of any phrases that should never be generated (sensitive tokens).

Deliverables and timing
- Smoke test: within 24 hours of receiving dataset (quick check to ensure format and basic coverage).
- Full run & initial report: 48-72 hours after dataset receipt. Report will include per-intent pass rates, confusion examples, latency breakdown, and recommendations.

If you'd like, I can run a short demo of the eval harness the day the data arrives so we can iterate quickly.

- Aditya
